claims.text: A hybrid high-throughput CALPHAD and machine-learning surrogate can accurately predict melting temperature, entropy of fusion, and heat capacity for multicomponent HEAs.
Mean elemental melting temperature and bulk modulus are useful ML descriptors for predicting HEA melting properties.
High-throughput CALPHAD can evaluate phase diagrams for 3-6-component equimolar alloys over approximately 600-3600 °C.
Rule-of-mixtures approaches fail because they neglect a nonlinear reduction in melting temperature as the number of components increases.
Rule-of-mixtures approaches underestimate the stability of solid solutions at high component count.
The number of distinct binary pairs in an N-component system is N(N-1)/2.
The increasing number of binary interactions with N depresses the melting temperature.
The increasing number of binary interactions with N stabilizes the solid-solution phase.
The vibrational entropy contribution in concentrated solid-solution alloys is approximately an order of magnitude smaller than configurational entropy.
Vibrational entropy is negligible in the entropy of fusion of HEAs.
The entropy of fusion in HEAs is dominated by configurational entropy and can be approximated by the configurational-entropy difference between liquid and solid.
Melting temperature decreases as component count increases because liquid structural complexity and unfavorable binary interactions preferentially stabilize the liquid through entropy.
An ML surrogate can bypass the cost of full CALPHAD while retaining accuracy in regimes where rule-of-mixtures fails.
Pure CALPHAD is computationally prohibitive for screening more than 100,000 compositions.
The method is valid for single-phase BCC, FCC, or HCP solid solutions and simple mixtures of solid solutions, but not for systems containing complex intermetallic precipitation.
The hybrid method will predict melting temperatures within 5% of CALPHAD for 5-6-component alloys.
Refractory-alloy melting temperature will decrease by approximately 100-200 °C for every additional principal element beyond N=3.
For single-phase solid solutions, entropy of fusion will be close to R ln N and will deviate primarily when intermetallics form.
The method will identify compositions with melting temperatures above 2000 °C and high entropy of fusion.
Prediction uncertainty increases above N=6 because the number of binary interaction parameters grows exponentially.

contradictions.description: The mediator correctly gives the binary-pair count as N(N-1)/2, which grows quadratically, whereas the uncertainty field calls its growth exponential.

The hypothesis states ΔSf ≈ ΔS_config, the mechanism defines it as the difference between liquid and solid configurational entropies, and the outcome predicts ΔSf ≈ R ln N. For equally disordered equimolar liquid and solid phases, both phases have approximately R ln N configurational entropy, so their difference would be near zero rather than R ln N.

The structural mediator says increasing binary interactions stabilize the solid solution, while the mechanism says unfavorable interactions lower the solid free energy less effectively and that the entropy term stabilizes the liquid; the direction of phase stabilization is therefore inconsistent.
